$meta.why: Corrects the reorganisation note UK Places supplies for the fourteen Lancashire councils. UK Places called two of the four groups 'East Lancashire' and 'West Lancashire (Fylde Coast)' and called the labels working geographic labels. The Secretary of State's decision letter of 16 July 2026 (p. 2) uses the proposal's names, North Lancashire, South Lancashire, Pennine Lancashire and Fylde Coast, and never uses East or West Lancashire as the name of a new council. West Lancashire is an existing district, which joins South Lancashire. Checked against the letter in Reports Public_Pound_work/phase0/GEOGRAPHY_LABELS.md, 4 October 2026.
$meta.applied: scripts/build-registry.mjs replaces place.reorganisation with the entry here for each GSS code listed, so a rebuild from UK Places keeps the correction. The fix also belongs upstream in UK Places.

E07000121.note: Under the four-unitary proposal the Secretary of State chose on 16 July 2026, Lancaster's area would join Preston and Ribble Valley in a new council that the proposal calls North Lancashire. The decision letter uses the proposal's names and does not name the new councils formally; it says a Structural Changes Order, subject to Parliamentary approval, is required. On 7 September 2026 the Secretary of State told the House of Commons that the July decisions for fourteen areas, Lancashire included, were paused pending a review.
